## Purpose

Download simple state outlines for **Texas** and **Michigan** with the
[`tigris`](https://github.com/walkerke/tigris) package and export each one as an
SVG file in this directory (`designs/coasters_blue_wave/`). The SVGs are sized
in millimetres so they import into Carbide Create at a known size.

A second section downloads **Michigan county** geometries and joins them to
county-level results from the **2026 U.S. Senate race** (Abdul El-Sayed vs.
Mike Rogers), read from the Michigan Secretary of State's results export, with
each candidate's share of the vote by county.

Notes on the choices below:

- `cb = TRUE` uses the Census *cartographic boundary* file, which is clipped to
  the shoreline. The full TIGER/Line state polygons include Great Lakes water,
  which would make Michigan look like a big block.
- `resolution = "20m"` is the most generalized version, which suits a 3" coaster
  and a 1/32" end mill.
- Each state is projected to a local equal-area / conformal CRS so the shape
  isn't stretched the way raw latitude/longitude would be.
- Small islands (Isle Royale, Beaver Island, the Texas barrier islands, etc.) are
  dropped below a size threshold. Set `min_part_frac <- 0` to keep everything.

## Download and export

```{r}
#| label: state-outlines

library(tigris)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# All files live in this document's folder. here::here() finds the project root
# (the .Rproj file) whether the document is rendered by Quarto or run
# chunk-by-chunk in RStudio, so paths work from either working directory.
out_dir <- here::here("designs", "coasters_blue_wave")

# Export settings ----------------------------------------------------------
width_mm      <- 45     # width of each exported outline in millimetres
min_part_frac <- 0.02   # drop polygon parts smaller than 2% of the largest part
simplify_m    <- 250    # extra simplification tolerance in metres (0 = none)

state_specs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,      ~abbr, ~crs,
  "texas",    "TX",  3083,   # NAD83 / Texas Centric Albers Equal Area
  "michigan", "MI",  3078    # NAD83 / Michigan Oblique Mercator
)

# Download -----------------------------------------------------------------
states_cb <- states(cb = TRUE, resolution = "20m", year = 2023)

# Helpers ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Keep the main land masses of a (multi)polygon; drop small islands
keep_main_parts <- function(geom, min_frac) {
  parts <- st_cast(st_geometry(geom), "POLYGON")
  areas <- as.numeric(st_area(parts))
  parts[areas >= min_frac * max(areas)] |> st_union()
}

# Write an sf polygon geometry (projected, metres) to an SVG sized in mm
write_state_svg <- function(geom, file, width_mm) {
  bb    <- st_bbox(geom)
  scale <- width_mm / as.numeric(bb["xmax"] - bb["xmin"])
  h_mm  <- as.numeric(bb["ymax"] - bb["ymin"]) * scale

  # one row per vertex; L1 = ring within polygon, L2 = polygon
  xy <- st_coordinates(st_cast(st_geometry(geom), "POLYGON"))
  xy <- as.data.frame(xy) |>
    mutate(x = (X - bb["xmin"]) * scale,
           y = (bb["ymax"] - Y) * scale)          # SVG y runs downward

  rings <- split(xy, list(xy$L2, xy$L1), drop = TRUE)
  d <- vapply(rings, function(r) {
    pts <- sprintf("%.3f,%.3f", r$x, r$y)
    paste0("M", pts[1], " L", paste(pts[-1], collapse = " "), " Z")
  }, character(1))

  svg <- c(
    '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no"?>',
    sprintf(paste0('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.1" ',
                   'width="%.3fmm" height="%.3fmm" viewBox="0 0 %.3f %.3f">'),
            width_mm, h_mm, width_mm, h_mm),
    sprintf('  <path d="%s" fill="black" fill-rule="evenodd" stroke="none"/>',
            paste(d, collapse = " ")),
    "</svg>"
  )
  writeLines(svg, file)
  invisible(c(width_mm = width_mm, height_mm = h_mm))
}

# Export -------------------------------------------------------------------
sizes <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(state_specs)), function(i) {
  s <- state_specs[i, ]
  geom <- states_cb |>
    filter(STUSPS == s$abbr) |>
    st_transform(s$crs) |>
    keep_main_parts(min_part_frac)
  if (simplify_m > 0) geom <- st_simplify(geom, preserveTopology = TRUE, dTolerance = simplify_m)

  file <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(s$name, "_outline.svg"))
  dims <- write_state_svg(geom, file, width_mm)
  tibble::tibble(state = s$name, file = file,
                 width_mm = dims[["width_mm"]], height_mm = round(dims[["height_mm"]], 1))
})
bind_rows(sizes)
```

```{r}
#| label: preview

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (s in state_specs$name) {
  states_cb |>
    filter(STUSPS == state_specs$abbr[state_specs$name == s]) |>
    st_transform(state_specs$crs[state_specs$name == s]) |>
    keep_main_parts(min_part_frac) |>
    plot(col = "grey20", border = NA, main = tools::toTitleCase(s))
}
```

## Michigan counties and 2026 U.S. Senate results

### County geometries

```{r}
#| label: mi-counties

mi_counties <- counties(state = "MI", cb = TRUE, resolution = "500k", year = 2023) |>
  st_transform(3078) |>                       # NAD83 / Michigan Oblique Mercator
  select(GEOID, county = NAME, geometry) |>
  arrange(county)

nrow(mi_counties)   # 83
```

### Election results

County results come straight from the Michigan Secretary of State's
tab-delimited export of **unofficial** results,
`data/2026STATE_GENERAL_MI_CENR_BY_COUNTY.txt` (one row per candidate per
office per county). The chunk keeps the U.S. Senate rows (`OfficeCode` 7),
totals El-Sayed, Rogers and all other candidates and write-ins for each county,
and joins them to the county geometries. Michigan's `CountyCode` numbers the 83
counties alphabetically, so the county FIPS code is `26000 + 2 * CountyCode - 1`;
the chunk also checks every county name against tigris.

**Data sources**

- Michigan Voter Information Center, county results for the November 3, 2026
  general election (source of the tab-delimited export):
  <https://mvic.sos.state.mi.us/votehistory/Index?type=C&electionDate=11-3-2026>
- Michigan Department of State, *Election Results and Data*:
  <https://www.michigan.gov/sos/elections/election-results-and-data>

These are preliminary, unofficial results until certified by the Michigan Board
of State Canvassers.

Re-download the file and render again to pick up later counts, including the
certified results once the Board of State Canvassers has met. A tidy county
summary is also written to `data/mi_senate_2026_by_county.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: senate-results

sos_file <- file.path(out_dir, "data", "2026STATE_GENERAL_MI_CENR_BY_COUNTY.txt")

sos <- read.delim(sos_file, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE,
                  quote = "", strip.white = TRUE)
names(sos) <- sub("\\(.*$", "", names(sos))      # "OfficeCode(text)" -> "OfficeCode"

results <- sos |>
  filter(OfficeCode == "7") |>                  # UNITED STATES SENATOR
  mutate(CandidateVotes = as.integer(CandidateVotes),
         candidate = case_when(CandidateLastName == "El-Sayed" ~ "el_sayed_votes",
                               CandidateLastName == "Rogers"   ~ "rogers_votes",
                               .default = "other_votes")) |>
  group_by(CountyCode, sos_county = CountyName, candidate) |>
  summarise(votes = sum(CandidateVotes), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = candidate, values_from = votes, values_fill = 0L) |>
  mutate(GEOID = sprintf("26%03d", 2L * as.integer(CountyCode) - 1L))

# vote shares and margin by county
results <- results |>
  mutate(total_votes  = el_sayed_votes + rogers_votes + other_votes,
         el_sayed_pct = 100 * el_sayed_votes / total_votes,
         rogers_pct   = 100 * rogers_votes   / total_votes,
         margin_pct   = el_sayed_pct - rogers_pct,          # + = El-Sayed ahead
         winner       = case_when(margin_pct > 0 ~ "El-Sayed",
                                  margin_pct < 0 ~ "Rogers",
                                  .default = NA_character_))

mi_senate <- mi_counties |> left_join(results, by = "GEOID")

# checks: all 83 counties matched, and names agree ("ST CLAIR" vs "St. Clair")
norm_name <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z]", "", x))
stopifnot(nrow(results) == 83,
          !anyNA(mi_senate$total_votes),
          all(norm_name(mi_senate$county) == norm_name(mi_senate$sos_county)))

# tidy county summary for reference / other tools
mi_senate |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(GEOID, county, el_sayed_votes, rogers_votes, other_votes, total_votes,
         el_sayed_pct, rogers_pct, margin_pct, winner) |>
  write.csv(file.path(out_dir, "data", "mi_senate_2026_by_county.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# statewide totals from the county rows
mi_senate |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(counties       = n(),
            el_sayed_votes = sum(el_sayed_votes),
            rogers_votes   = sum(rogers_votes),
            other_votes    = sum(other_votes),
            total_votes    = sum(total_votes)) |>
  mutate(el_sayed_pct = round(100 * el_sayed_votes / total_votes, 2),
         rogers_pct   = round(100 * rogers_votes   / total_votes, 2))
```

### County table

```{r}
#| label: senate-table

mi_senate |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  transmute(county, el_sayed_votes, el_sayed_pct = round(el_sayed_pct, 1),
            rogers_votes, rogers_pct = round(rogers_pct, 1),
            margin_pct = round(margin_pct, 1), winner) |>
  arrange(desc(margin_pct))
```

### Map

```{r}
#| label: senate-map
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 8

lim <- max(abs(mi_senate$margin_pct))
pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#b2182b", "#f7f7f7", "#2166ac"))(21)   # Rogers - even - El-Sayed
plot(mi_senate["margin_pct"], pal = pal, breaks = seq(-lim, lim, length.out = 22),
     border = "white", lwd = 0.3,
     main = "2026 U.S. Senate, Michigan (unofficial): El-Sayed minus Rogers, pct. points")
```

### GeoJSON export

Two GeoJSON files are written to `data/`, in WGS84 longitude/latitude
(EPSG:4326, as the GeoJSON standard expects), each with the county vote totals,
shares, margin and winner as attributes:

- `mi_counties_senate_2026.geojson` - all 83 Michigan counties
- `mi_counties_el_sayed_advantage_2026.geojson` - only the counties where
  El-Sayed led Rogers (`margin_pct > 0`)

```{r}
#| label: geojson-export

geo_out <- mi_senate |>
  select(GEOID, county, el_sayed_votes, rogers_votes, other_votes, total_votes,
         el_sayed_pct, rogers_pct, margin_pct, winner) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_pct"), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  st_transform(4326)

all_file <- file.path(out_dir, "data", "mi_counties_senate_2026.geojson")
es_file  <- file.path(out_dir, "data", "mi_counties_el_sayed_advantage_2026.geojson")

st_write(geo_out, all_file, driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
st_write(filter(geo_out, margin_pct > 0), es_file,
         driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

tibble::tibble(file     = basename(c(all_file, es_file)),
               counties = c(nrow(geo_out), sum(geo_out$margin_pct > 0)))
```

### SVG export

The same two county sets are also exported as SVG, like the state outlines:
sized in millimetres (`width_mm` wide) for Carbide Create, with each county as
its own closed path (`id` = county name). Both files share the full-Michigan
frame, so the El-Sayed counties line up exactly when laid over the all-counties
file. Island parts that aren't part of the main state outline (Isle Royale,
Beaver Island, etc.) are dropped, and lines are simplified by `simplify_m`.

- `mi_counties_senate_2026.svg` - all 83 counties
- `mi_counties_el_sayed_advantage_2026.svg` - counties where El-Sayed led

```{r}
#| label: svg-export

# main land masses of Michigan (same island rule as the state outline)
mi_main <- states_cb |>
  filter(STUSPS == "MI") |>
  st_transform(3078) |>
  keep_main_parts(min_part_frac)

# drop county parts that don't touch the main state outline, then simplify
county_shapes <- mi_senate |>
  select(GEOID, county, margin_pct) |>
  st_cast("POLYGON", warn = FALSE)
county_shapes <- county_shapes[lengths(st_intersects(county_shapes, mi_main)) > 0, ] |>
  group_by(GEOID, county, margin_pct) |>
  summarise(.groups = "drop")
if (simplify_m > 0) {
  county_shapes <- st_simplify(county_shapes, preserveTopology = TRUE, dTolerance = simplify_m)
}

# Write each feature as its own outlined path, in a shared frame (bbox) sized in mm
write_features_svg <- function(x, file, width_mm, bbox, id_col = "county") {
  scale <- width_mm / as.numeric(bbox["xmax"] - bbox["xmin"])
  h_mm  <- as.numeric(bbox["ymax"] - bbox["ymin"]) * scale

  paths <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(x)), function(i) {
    xy <- as.data.frame(st_coordinates(st_cast(st_geometry(x[i, ]), "POLYGON"))) |>
      mutate(px = (X - bbox["xmin"]) * scale,
             py = (bbox["ymax"] - Y) * scale)            # SVG y runs downward
    rings <- split(xy, list(xy$L2, xy$L1), drop = TRUE)
    d <- vapply(rings, function(r) {
      pts <- sprintf("%.3f,%.3f", r$px, r$py)
      paste0("M", pts[1], " L", paste(pts[-1], collapse = " "), " Z")
    }, character(1))
    sprintf('  <path id="%s" d="%s"/>', x[[id_col]][i], paste(d, collapse = " "))
  }, character(1))

  writeLines(c(
    '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no"?>',
    sprintf(paste0('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.1" ',
                   'width="%.3fmm" height="%.3fmm" viewBox="0 0 %.3f %.3f">'),
            width_mm, h_mm, width_mm, h_mm),
    '<g fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="0.1" stroke-linejoin="round">',
    paths,
    "</g>",
    "</svg>"), file)
  invisible(c(width_mm = width_mm, height_mm = h_mm))
}

frame <- st_bbox(county_shapes)                 # full Michigan frame for both files
svg_all <- file.path(out_dir, "data", "mi_counties_senate_2026.svg")
svg_es  <- file.path(out_dir, "data", "mi_counties_el_sayed_advantage_2026.svg")

write_features_svg(county_shapes, svg_all, width_mm, frame)
write_features_svg(filter(county_shapes, margin_pct > 0), svg_es, width_mm, frame)

tibble::tibble(file     = basename(c(svg_all, svg_es)),
               counties = c(nrow(county_shapes), sum(county_shapes$margin_pct > 0)))
```

## Congress by party, 2024 vs. 2026

A 2x2 matrix of pie charts (rows = chamber: Senate, House; columns = year:
2024, 2026) showing the share of seats held by each party, exported as
`congress_party_share_2024_2026.svg` in this folder. "Other" covers
independents; shares are computed within each chamber and year (100 Senate
seats, 435 House seats).

The SVG is plain line geometry for engraving, sized in millimetres like the
other exports, with no text or colour:

- each pie is a circle outline plus radial lines at the slice boundaries
  (slices start at 12 o'clock and run clockwise: Republican, Democratic, Other)
- **Republican** slices: single-direction hatching (45 degrees)
- **Democratic** slices: cross-hatching (45 and 135 degrees)
- **Other** slices: no hatching

Lines are grouped (`outlines`, `hatch_republican`, `hatch_democratic`) so each
set can be given its own toolpath.

```{r}
#| label: congress-party-share

congress <- tibble::tribble(
  ~chamber, ~year, ~party,       ~seats,
  "Senate", 2024,  "Republican", 53,
  "Senate", 2024,  "Democratic", 45,
  "Senate", 2024,  "Other",       2,
  "Senate", 2026,  "Republican", 44,
  "Senate", 2026,  "Democratic", 54,
  "Senate", 2026,  "Other",       2,
  "House",  2024,  "Republican", 220,
  "House",  2024,  "Democratic", 215,
  "House",  2024,  "Other",       0,
  "House",  2026,  "Republican", 178,
  "House",  2026,  "Democratic", 257,
  "House",  2026,  "Other",       0
) |>
  group_by(chamber, year) |>
  mutate(share = seats / sum(seats)) |>
  ungroup()

# Layout (mm) --------------------------------------------------------------
pie_d_mm   <- 30      # diameter of each pie
pie_gap_mm <- 8       # space between pies
margin_mm  <- 2       # space around the grid
hatch_mm   <- 2.5     # hatch line spacing (coarse)
line_w_mm  <- 0.3     # stroke width (display only)

party_order <- c("Republican", "Democratic", "Other")
hatch_angles <- list(Republican = 45, Democratic = c(45, 135), Other = numeric(0))
rows <- c("Senate", "House")
cols <- c(2024, 2026)

r_mm   <- pie_d_mm / 2
size_w <- 2 * margin_mm + length(cols) * pie_d_mm + (length(cols) - 1) * pie_gap_mm
size_h <- 2 * margin_mm + length(rows) * pie_d_mm + (length(rows) - 1) * pie_gap_mm

# Geometry helpers (SVG space: x right, y down; angles clockwise from 12 o'clock)
pie_pt <- function(cx, cy, r, a) cbind(cx + r * sin(a), cy - r * cos(a))

slice_poly <- function(cx, cy, r, a0, a1) {
  arc <- pie_pt(cx, cy, r, seq(a0, a1, length.out = max(3, ceiling((a1 - a0) / 0.02))))
  st_polygon(list(rbind(c(cx, cy), arc, c(cx, cy))))
}

# parallel lines at angle `deg` (0 = horizontal) covering a circle, spaced `step`
hatch_lines <- function(cx, cy, r, deg, step) {
  th <- deg * pi / 180
  u  <- c(cos(th), -sin(th))            # line direction (y flipped for SVG)
  n  <- c(sin(th),  cos(th))            # normal
  offs <- seq(-r, r, by = step)
  offs <- offs - mean(offs)             # centre the pattern on the pie
  st_multilinestring(lapply(offs, function(o) {
    p <- c(cx, cy) + o * n
    rbind(p - 1.5 * r * u, p + 1.5 * r * u)
  }))
}

lines_d <- function(g) {
  if (is.null(g) || st_is_empty(g)) return(character(0))
  xy <- as.data.frame(st_coordinates(g))
  grp <- if ("L2" %in% names(xy)) interaction(xy$L1, xy$L2, drop = TRUE) else xy$L1
  vapply(split(xy, grp), function(l)
    paste0("M", paste(sprintf("%.3f,%.3f", l$X, l$Y), collapse = " L")), character(1))
}

# Build the paths ----------------------------------------------------------
outline_d <- character(0)
hatch_d   <- list(Republican = character(0), Democratic = character(0))

for (i in seq_along(rows)) for (j in seq_along(cols)) {
  cx <- margin_mm + r_mm + (j - 1) * (pie_d_mm + pie_gap_mm)
  cy <- margin_mm + r_mm + (i - 1) * (pie_d_mm + pie_gap_mm)

  d <- congress |>
    filter(chamber == rows[i], year == cols[j], seats > 0) |>
    mutate(party = factor(party, levels = party_order)) |>
    arrange(party) |>
    mutate(a1 = 2 * pi * cumsum(share), a0 = a1 - 2 * pi * share)

  # circle outline + radial boundaries (none if one party holds every seat)
  circ <- pie_pt(cx, cy, r_mm, seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 241))
  outline_d <- c(outline_d,
                 paste0("M", paste(sprintf("%.3f,%.3f", circ[, 1], circ[, 2]), collapse = " L"), " Z"))
  if (nrow(d) > 1) {
    for (a in d$a0) {
      e <- pie_pt(cx, cy, r_mm, a)
      outline_d <- c(outline_d, sprintf("M%.3f,%.3f L%.3f,%.3f", cx, cy, e[1], e[2]))
    }
  }

  # hatching clipped to each slice
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(d))) {
    p <- as.character(d$party[k])
    if (length(hatch_angles[[p]]) == 0) next
    sl <- slice_poly(cx, cy, r_mm, d$a0[k], d$a1[k])
    for (deg in hatch_angles[[p]]) {
      hatch_d[[p]] <- c(hatch_d[[p]], lines_d(st_intersection(hatch_lines(cx, cy, r_mm, deg, hatch_mm), sl)))
    }
  }
}

# Write the SVG -------------------------------------------------------------
grp <- function(id, d) c(sprintf('<g id="%s">', id), sprintf('  <path d="%s"/>', d), "</g>")
writeLines(c(
  '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no"?>',
  sprintf(paste0('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.1" ',
                 'width="%.3fmm" height="%.3fmm" viewBox="0 0 %.3f %.3f">'),
          size_w, size_h, size_w, size_h),
  sprintf('<g fill="none" stroke="black" stroke-width="%.2f" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">',
          line_w_mm),
  grp("hatch_republican", hatch_d$Republican),
  grp("hatch_democratic", hatch_d$Democratic),
  grp("outlines", outline_d),
  "</g>",
  "</svg>"), file.path(out_dir, "congress_party_share_2024_2026.svg"))

c(width_mm = size_w, height_mm = size_h)
```
